title: Branching Incident Example
briefing: A suspicious security event begins to unfold across the environment.

injects.title: Threat Intelligence Update
injects.message: External reporting suggests the phishing pattern matches a known campaign associated with credential theft and rapid follow-on activity.

injects.title: Leadership Pressure
injects.message: Business leaders request an immediate status update and ask whether additional teams should prepare for operational disruption.

injects.title: Identity Control Review
injects.message: IAM confirms recent suspicious sign-in activity tied to the same users involved in the initial reports.

step1.situation: A suspicious email is reported by multiple users.

if_correct.consequence: The email is escalated quickly and investigation begins early.

if_incorrect.consequence: The threat is underestimated and spreads further.

step2_fast.situation: The team validates suspicious indicators while containment begins.

if_correct.consequence: Indicators are confirmed and the threat is narrowed quickly.

if_incorrect.consequence: Investigation loses clarity and threat confidence drops.

step2_slow.situation: Delayed escalation creates confusion across the organization.

if_correct.consequence: The team recovers some control through faster communication.

if_incorrect.consequence: The incident escalates and disrupts more business units.

step3_contained.situation: Identity protections are reviewed as part of successful containment.

if_correct.consequence: Identity controls reinforce recovery and reduce further abuse.

if_incorrect.consequence: Weak identity handling leaves some residual risk.

step3_partial.situation: Leadership requests a formal policy response during partial containment.

if_incorrect.consequence: Lack of policy clarity weakens response coordination.

step3_outbreak.situation: The incident has now spread enough to affect business continuity.

if_correct.consequence: A strong late response limits further escalation.

if_incorrect.consequence: Containment fails and the incident becomes a major outage.
